title: Void Ending in a Sextile to Saturn
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3, Book III chapter 1 and Book III chapter 8

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The sextile is one of the two friendly aspects. Picatrix ties the Moon to the fortunes by trine and sextile whenever a work is meant to prosper, and grades the sextile as the aspect of moderate friendship: the signs it joins are kin in action but not in passion, so the concord between them is a lukewarm one.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a sextile to Saturn, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his weight and his cold. Saturn holds the power of retention, and when he is afflicted he is the gravest of the impediments: the science of law and profound knowledge, deep and occult properties, the building trades, and working the soil are his, with murky rivers, black mountains, deep wells, and desert places among his locations. Lead and iron are his metals, black his color, the bitter taste his own. Well disposed and direct, he gives purity, long life, standing, honor, riches, and durable inheritances; afflicted, he is the lord of poverty, misery, pain, and imprisonment.
